metadata.name: patch
metadata.displayName: patch - Apply a diff to files
metadata.description: Apply changes described by a diff file

installation.note: patch is commonly installed by default on many Linux systems; if missing, install via your package manager (e.g., sudo apt install patch)

overview.summary: The patch command applies changes to files based on a diff (often in unified diff format). It's used heavily in development workflows, for applying fixes, updating source trees, or consuming patches from email/issue trackers.
when_to_use: Apply a unified diff (.patch/.diff) to source code
Update a directory tree using a patch set

syntax.description: Most commonly, you pass the patch through stdin and run patch in the target directory.

options.description: Strip NUM leading components from file paths in the patch
options.use_case: When patch paths include prefixes like a/ and b/ (common in git diffs)

options.description: Apply the patch in reverse (attempt to undo changes)
options.use_case: To revert a patch you previously applied

options.description: Check whether the patch would apply cleanly without modifying files
options.use_case: Preview whether the patch will apply before changing anything

examples.title: Apply a git-style patch
examples.description: Apply a patch file that contains paths like a/file and b/file
examples.use_case: Apply changes exported from git or sent by someone else

examples.title: Test a patch before applying
examples.description: Verify the patch can be applied cleanly without modifying files
examples.use_case: Avoid partially-applied patches and messy rollback

common_pitfalls.description: If file paths in the patch don't match your directory structure, patch will fail to find files.
common_pitfalls.solution: Try different -p values (commonly -p1 for git diffs). Inspect the patch header paths to choose correctly.

common_pitfalls.description: If the target files have changed since the patch was created, hunks may fail.
common_pitfalls.solution: Apply with --dry-run first, then manually resolve rejects (*.rej) if needed.

related_commands.description: Generate diffs that patch can apply
Git can produce/apply patches (git format-patch / git apply), often used instead of patch in repos
